rule.title: Comments Must Explain 'Why', Never 'What'
rule.statement: In-line comments must explain technical rationale, non-obvious business requirements, or architectural trade-offs; they must never simply narrate the code.
rule.rationale: Narrative comments (// increment i by 1) become outdated quickly, pollute the file, and distract from the actual logic.
rule.implementation_guidance: If code is not obvious, refactor variable and function names. Use comments only for rationale (e.g., // Overlap is set to 50 words to bridge cross-page sentences).

forbidden.example: // Split the document into chunks const chunks = split(text);

preferred.example: // 50-word overlap bridges boundary sentences in legal contracts that span page breaks

source.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
source.evidence_quote: Comments do not make up for bad code. Clear and expressive code with few comments is far superior to a cluttered and complex code with lots of comments.
